name: GOLF
description: Golf is a card game for two or more players where the object is to score as little as possible, like the sport. Each player has a layout of face-down cards that can be replaced by drawing from stock or discard piles. The game is commonly played over 9 or 18 deals ('holes'), with the lowest total score winning. Also known as Polish Polka, Polish Poker, Turtle (4-card), Hara Kiri (6-card), or Crazy Nines (9-card).

Each player has a layout of face-down cards that can be replaced by drawing from stock or discard piles. The game is commonly played over 9 or 18 deals ('holes'), with the lowest total score winning. Also known as Polish Polka, Polish Poker, Turtle (4-card), Hara Kiri (6-card), or Crazy Nines (9-card).

Country/Region of Origin: USA/UK
Time Period: Early-to-mid 20th century
Creator(s): Unknown (folk game)
Etymology: Named after the sport of golf where lower scores are better; scores represent 'strokes' taken to play a hole

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 8 (use 2 decks for 8+ players)
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: No

Type: Standard 52-card
Number of Decks: 1 (2 for 8+ players)
Jokers: Optional (variations)

Standard deck of cards
Score sheet for tracking over multiple holes

4-Card Golf: 4 cards each, arranged in square, 2 face-up to view
6-Card Golf: 6 cards each, arranged 2x3, some variations start with all face down
8-Card Golf: 8 cards each
Remaining cards form stock pile; top card turned for discard pile

items.text: Four-Card Golf: Each player has four cards in a square, two of which may be looked at once before play. Player may knock to end the hand after others get one more turn. Also known as Turtle.
Six-Card Golf: Six cards per player in a 2x3 layout. Replacement cards are placed face up. Play ends when any player has all six cards face up; others get one more turn. Also known as Hara Kiri.
Eight-Card Golf: Eight cards per player; layout and play similar to six-card. Play ends when one player's layout is fully face up.
Nine-Card Golf: Nine cards in a 3x3 grid. Same draw-and-replace flow; play ends when any player has all cards face up. Three of a kind in a column score zero. Also known as Crazy Nines.
Ten-Card Golf: Ten cards per player; less common. Same draw-and-replace mechanic; end condition typically when one player's layout is fully face up.

Golf with Power Cards: Four-card Golf variant (Cambio, Cabo, Pablo, Cactus, Dacz) where certain cards drawn from the stock grant special powers (peek at a card, swap with opponent, etc.); used or discarded as normal if taken from the discard pile.
Single-deck Golf: Played with one deck for two to four players. Rules match the chosen layout (e.g. four-card or six-card); sometimes jokers are not used.

Knocking variant: In four-card style, a player may knock instead of drawing to end the hand; each other player gets one final turn. Knocker may be penalised if not lowest, or rewarded if lowest (e.g. score zero).
